# Credits

The Hunted is developed by **Umutcan Ekinci**
([GitHub](https://github.com/umutcanekinci) · [itch.io](https://umutcanekinci.itch.io)) and
published by VectorViolet.

The game's code is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). The game is built with third-party
assets and software, credited below with their licenses. Thank you to everyone who makes their
work freely available. Some older assets have no confirmed source yet; they are listed honestly
under "Pending replacement" and are not covered by the MIT license.

### Attribution

- Four characters: My LPC entries ([CC BY 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/)): Stephen "Redshrike" Challener, with a link to https://opengameart.org
- 8-Bit Beat'em Up Soundtrack ([CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)): "8-Bit Beat'em Up Soundtrack" by wyver9

### Pending replacement

78 files have no confirmed source or license. They are not credited to anyone and are not covered by the MIT license; each is being replaced or tracked down:

- `assets/images/buttons/` (7 files): replace (owner, 2026-11-20): made with an online button generator, and the start button is a free-PNG-site image
- `assets/images/cursor/` (52 files): replace (owner, 2026-11-20): source not found (a Pikachu cursor, so not usable)
- `assets/images/vampire/` (18 files): replace (owner, 2026-11-20): generate a new vampire with AI image generation, in the game's new art style
- `assets/sounds/jump.wav` (1 file): replaced on 2026-07-09 (commit 4aedf04) without a recorded source: find it, or replace it

CC0 assets need no attribution; they are credited here anyway. The OFL font is
bundled unmodified with its license text. CC BY and CC BY-SA assets require
attribution (see above). Each pack's own license text ships with the game: `licenses/assets/amir027-platform-tile4.txt`, `licenses/assets/ansimuz-mountain-at-dusk.txt`, `licenses/assets/font-comic-neue.txt`, `licenses/assets/redshrike-lpc-four-characters.txt`, `licenses/assets/wyver9-8bit-beatem-up.txt`.
[assets/SOURCES.yaml](https://github.com/vectorviolet/hunted/blob/main/assets/SOURCES.yaml) in the source repository lists every asset
file with its pack and its original file name there.

## Software

| Software | License |
|---|---|
| [pygame-ce](https://pyga.me) | [GNU LGPL 2.1](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/lgpl-2.1.html) |
| [pygamine](https://github.com/vectorviolet/pygamine) (the game's engine layer) | [MIT](https://github.com/vectorviolet/pygamine/blob/main/LICENSE) |
| [Python](https://www.python.org) | [PSF License](https://docs.python.org/3/license.html) |
| [PyInstaller](https://pyinstaller.org) (builds the standalone bundles) | [GPL 2.0 with a bootloader exception](https://github.com/pyinstaller/pyinstaller/blob/develop/COPYING.txt) |
| Native libraries bundled with pygame-ce: SDL 2 and its image, mixer and ttf libraries, FreeType, libpng, libjpeg, libtiff, libwebp, zlib, Ogg/Vorbis, Opus, WavPack, libxmp, PortMidi and, on macOS and Linux, FLAC, HarfBuzz, Brotli, mpg123, libsndfile and FluidSynth | zlib, BSD, MIT, FreeType, LGPL 2.1 and others, each listed in `licenses/README.md` |

The license texts of pygame-ce, pygamine and the native libraries ship with the game in
`licenses/`, starting with
`licenses/pygame-ce.txt`, `licenses/pygamine.txt` and `licenses/sdl2.txt`; `licenses/README.md`
maps every library to its text. The asset packs' license texts are in `licenses/assets/`.

The startup splash shows the pygame-ce “powered” logo, which the pygame-ce project
[offers for use in game projects](https://pyga.me/docs/logos.html).
